MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 10, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:01 p.m., on September 10, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 6, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way and at 1405 Ocean Avenue, Seal
Beach, CA 90740 (Council Member Kelley’s teleconference location).

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley(arrived via teleconference from Seal Beach, CA at 6:38 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator, Government Code Section 54956.8. The
  property commonly referred to as “Casta del Sol Golf Course” located at 27601 Casta
  del Sol, Mission Viejo, California. City of Mission Viejo Negotiators: City Manager
  Dennis Wilberg, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay,
  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas and City Attorney William Curley,
  III. Negotiating Party: Professional Real Estate Services (PRES) President Brad
  Schroth. Under discussion price and terms.

City Council Minutes  1  September 10, 2019
 CS2. Liability Claims: Claimants: Donaldson, Orloff, Gray and O’Brien: Agency Claimed
  Against-City of Mission Viejo and: Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to
  Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9. (4 cases).

RECESS TO COSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council discussed two closed session items. CS1
was related to real property negotiations and updates were received and direction was given to
staff but no reportable action occurred. He said CS2 related to liability claims but only one was
discussed. The Council was updated as to the state of the claim and the legal proceedings involved,
but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Musical Performance by the Mini Jimmy’s

  The Mini Jimmy’s performed for the Council and audience.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Kenzo Katayama, MV: Suggested that the City consider a monthly Intercoastal Cleanup Day.

Jetta Baptiste, MV: Discussed the recent devastating hurricane in the Bahamas and asked the City
to support a charity for the victims of the hurricane.

Jacklyn Flowers, LN: Spoke about the Bahamas hurricane and the financial loss for the country.
She announced that the GoFundMe page for support to the hurricane victims is
www.gofundme.com/f/dorian-assistance-for-grand-bahama-bahamas.

Cathy Schlicht, MV: Expressed dissatisfaction with the City’s handling of the California Voting
Rights Act lawsuit. She questioned why the Voter Education Ad Hoc Committee has not met in
over nine months and voiced concern over the increasing legal costs and the lack of communication
with voters.

Mark Shubert, MV: Apologized to the residents that live in the vicinity of the Marguerite Aquatics
Center for the increased noise over the summer. He outlined the remedies that will be made to
reduce noise and lighting.

City Council Minutes  2  September 10, 2019
 CONSENT CALENDAR

*Note: At 6:38 p.m., Council Member Kelley joined the meeting via teleconference from Seal
Beach, CA.

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 27, 2019, as presented.

2.  Check Register dated August 23, 2019 in the amount of $3,774,590.24

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2019

  Received and filed.

4.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for July 2019

  Received and filed.

5.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for July 2019

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2019

  Received and filed.

7.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2018/19

  Received and filed the accompanying City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year
  2018/19.

8.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report for
  Fiscal Year 2018/19

  Received and filed the accompanying CDFA Treasurer's Annual Report for FY 2018/19.
City Council Minutes  3  September 10, 2019
 9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA)Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year
  2018/19

  Received and filed the accompanying MVHA Treasurer's Annual Report for FY 2018/19.

10. FY 2019/20 Investment Policies

  Adopted Resolution 19-26 Approving the City’s Investment Policy for FY 2019/20, CDFA
  Resolution 19-27 Approving the Authority's Investment Policy for FY 2019/20, and
  Housing Authority Resolution 19-28 Approving the Mission Viejo Housing Authority
  Investment Policy for FY 2019/20.

11. Christopher Park Play Area Renovations – CIP 19312

  (1) Awarded contract to Jeff Tracy, Inc: Land Forms Landscape Construction (A19-45) for
  the Christopher Park Play Area Renovations - CIP 19312, in an amount not to exceed
  $433,361.00; (2) approved issuance of Purchase Orders for the purchase and delivery of play
  equipment for Christopher Park Area Renovations –CIP 19312 to the following vendors in
  the related not to exceed amounts: Dave Bang Associates, Inc. $96,198.16; Land Rec
  $7,802.17; Innovative Playgrounds Company, Inc. $8,230.86; Coast Recreation, Inc.
  $8,248.41; Great Western Recreation (GameTime), $9,754.46; and (3) adopted Resolution
  19-29 Amending the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Budget for Costs Related to CIP 19312.

12. Maintenance of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance, Interconnect, Battery Back-Up
  Systems, Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights and CCTV Cameras

  (1) Awarded the contract for the subject services to Bear Electrical Solutions, Inc., (A19-46)
  for the period October 1, 2019, to June 30, 2021, in the amount of $805,000; and (2)
  authorized issuance of a purchase order to Bear Electrical Solutions, Inc., for the period
  October 1, 2019, to June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $345,000.

13. Federal Transportation Improvement Program

  Adopted Resolution 19-30 Certifying that the City of Mission Viejo Has the Resources to
  Fund the Projects in the FFY 2020/21–2025/26 Transportation Improvement Program and
  Affirming Its Commitment to Implement All Projects in the Program.

14. CUSD Supplemental Joint Facility Use Agreement No. 3 to include Castille, Pavion,
  and Cordova Parks.

  Approved the CUSD Supplemental Joint Facility Use Agreement No. 3 (A94-05).

15. Contract Renewal with Mercy House Living Centers for Homeless Outreach Services

  (1) Approved Mercy House Living Centers (A19-47) Contract for Homeless Outreach
  Services; and (2) adopted Resolution 19-31 Amending the FY 19/20 Police Services Budget.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  4  September 10, 2019
 OLD BUSINESS

16. Energy Efficient Measures Fee Waiver for New City Residents and Seniors

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister gave the staff report.
  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve new energy efficient fee waiver program to benefit seniors and new homeowners in
  Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

17. Casta Del Sol Golf Course Update

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the update

  Alan Dibartolomeo, PRES, Irvine: Encouraged the Council to partner with PRES in
  managing the golf course.

  Anthony Elia, MV: Suggested the Council hire an independent group of experts in the
  decision-making process for the golf course to include a forensic accountant CPA. He stated
  that it would be beneficial if the City hired a professional golf course maintenance chief to
  inspect the property and submit a report and he recommended the possibility of a three-year
  lease with option to purchase at the end of 18 months.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

City Council Minutes  5  September 10, 2019
 Council Member Bucknum

Addressing the Saddleback College Students in the audience, Council Member Bucknum
discussed her reasons for running for City Council and her history with Community Services
Commission. She stated that she attended the retirement party for Santa Margarita Water District
Board Member Charlie Wilson and concerts in the park and at Lake Mission Viejo. Council
Member Bucknum asked the City Attorney to explain the California Voting Rights Act (CVRA)
to the students in the audience and Mr. Curley gave a summary and the City’s actions related to
the CVRA. In closing, Council Member Bucknum announced that the City will hold a Patriot Day
ceremony at the Norman P. Murray Community Center at 6:00 p.m. on September 11.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley addressed the Saddleback College students and explained why she ran for
City Council. She gave a shout out to Cathy Allen who was honored for the City’s Wall of
Recognition at the Community Center. She also discussed her attendance, along with a few of the
City Commissioners, at the Vocational Visions Enchanted Evening fundraiser.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs asked the City Manager to publish the Economic Impact Report on the
Nadadores Swimming events on the City's website. He asked every resident in Mission Viejo to
attend the 9/11 ceremonies at their local fire station at 9:00 a.m. to honor the victims of 9/11/2001.
Council Member Sachs concluded with his reasons for running for City Council to inform the
Saddleback College students in the audience.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell highlighted the Economic Impact Report on the swim events at the
Marguerite Aquatics Complex. He stated that the Junior Olympics economic impact was roughly
$300,000 for the City, and the U.S. Swimming Masters was $471,269. He announced that he is
excited for the new Saddleback College Stadium and all the future sporting events that can be held
there and he touched on the many events that were held at the Marguerite Aquatics Center this past
summer. Addressing the students in the audience, Mayor Pro Tem Goodell discussed his reasons
for running for City Council. He also noted that as part of the Olympic Promotion Committee, he
met with Recreation and Community Services Director Mark Nix and some volunteers from the
Special Olympics to discuss the City hosting a Special Olympics Home Town Event. The one-
day event would provide an opportunity to compliment the City’s SNAP (Special Needs Adaptive
Programming) and the event would be promoted to Mission Viejo Athletes and would include a
Unity Torch Walk. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell asked that staff work with Director Nix and research
the opportunity with the Special Olympics.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths announced that it is Restaurant Week in the City until September 15. He stated that
the “Buy Local Campaign” Expo is September 19, 2019, in the Village Center Parking lot from
4:30 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. He also invited residents to the Rotary Club breakfast tomorrow morning
at 7:00 a.m. In closing, Mayor Raths thanked Jacklyn Flowers for her concern for her family and
friends in the Bahamas.
City Council Minutes  6  September 10, 2019
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:43 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 24, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 24, 2019

City Council Minutes  7  September 10, 2019
